title: Masking, paths and strokes
objective: Make brush masks safe to paint on — the occupancy cap refused on the stroke that crosses it and a decimation that keeps ordinary painting under it — make the path limits agree, get the kind table ready for the next kinds, cut paint latency where the measurement points, store only new strokes, type the mask commands, and prove each mask property once; then generalize the path primitives before Corrections needs them.
context_summary: Masks run on the one action path, the component-kind table dispatches validate and compile, the desktop has one shape editor per drawn kind, and strokes are content-addressed and shared, with coverage bit-identical to its frozen f64 reference. The 64-segments-per-cell occupancy cap was never measured on real painting and is enforced only when a layer first draws the mask, so ordinary strokes commit and it is the next masked adjustment that gets refused. Paint latency misses its bound for reasons outside the mask mathematics, and the mask tests — about 21,000 lines against roughly 12,000 lines of production — repeat each kind's checklist by hand and keep reference studies inside the core's own test binary. The path primitives a brush stroke is built from are still the mask's own, and both the next proposed kind and the Corrections brush need them generalized.

tasks.description: Refuse a brush stroke that would push any grid cell over the 64-segment occupancy cap at the moment it is painted, and add a core test that measures maximum cell occupancy from a realistic scrub.
extra_context: Wave 1, fix. The owner made the occupancy cap's future conditional on a measurement that was never taken, and this is the largest correctness risk found in masking.

`SEGMENTS_PER_PIXEL` (64, in `mask/brush.rs`) is enforced only inside `Compiled::new`, reached through `compile`, which `modules/registry/compile.rs` runs only for a mask some layer's `mask` field actually names (the test `the_mask_table_is_checked_on_admission_and_not_by_compile` confirms an undrawn mask is never compiled). `brush::validate`, which every `mask.add-stroke` goes through at admission, only calls `parse` and never builds the index. So every stroke committed to a mask no layer yet draws is accepted regardless of occupancy, and the refusal only surfaces later, on the first adjustment that binds a layer to that mask — and stays refused until strokes are deleted, since `Compiled::new` runs again on every compile.

A faithful port of the index build (`Index::build`, `decimate_to_grid`) into a standalone simulation shows ordinary hand-drawn painting exceeds the cap: 67–185 for one six-pass scrub with 1 px jitter, 73–364 for six overlapping strokes, and 165–181 for eight short arcs at the default brush size. Every shipped brush measurement is a straight or collinear path instead (the `mask-brush` smoke's 2-point strokes, the latency workload's collinear path decimating to 2 points), so no curved stroke has ever been compiled in evidence.

Owner decision (2026-09-26): a stroke that would cross the cap is refused when it is painted, not when a layer first draws the mask; the cap itself stays at 64 segments per cell, and a stroke that reaches it does not spill into a new component, because components combine by the Zadeh maximum rather than a stroke-screen union, so a spill would silently stop that area's painting from building up further.

The claim in `brush.rs` that "a brush that could not be evaluated cannot be committed either" is false for a mask no layer draws yet; correct or remove it, and give `mask::rules` an entry for this refusal so the panel can state it before a stroke is even sent.
Coverage of every stroke that does commit stays bit-identical to its f64 reference: neither the fold nor the per-stroke equation changes here, only where the cap is checked.

tasks.description: Decimate a captured stroke with a tolerance relative to its brush radius, sized from the scrub measurement, so ordinary painting stays under the 64-segment occupancy cap.
extra_context: Wave 1, fix. This is the remedy the previous task's scrub measurement exists to size, and it is the option the owner chose over raising the cap or spilling to a new component.

Today `decimate_to_grid` (`path.rs`) keeps any point that deviates by more than `DECIMATION_TOLERANCE` — 2 grid steps, 0.49 px at 4000 px stage height — regardless of the stroke's own radius, and screen-quantized pointer positions routinely deviate by more than that. The occupancy cell side is the component's largest radius, and a segment enters every cell its radius-grown box reaches (about 3 cells per axis), so one cell counts every segment within roughly 1.5 R of it: a fixed pixel tolerance stores far more segments per cell for a small brush than a large one.

The scrub simulation shows a relative tolerance of 1–2% of the brush radius cuts the worst measured occupancy from 185 to 19 and from 364 to 58, and roughly halves the number of stored points, at the brush sizes the previous task measured.

This changes what a new capture stores — the decimation contract in docs/design/masking.md ("Storing a path") and `path.rs` — which current shapes only allows: no migration or old-stroke compatibility is needed, only a stored contract met the same way going forward.

Coverage of every stroke, old or newly captured, stays bit-identical to its f64 reference, because the fold and the per-stroke equation are untouched; only how many points a new capture keeps changes.

tasks.description: Apply the 1,024-position stroke limit after decimation as the design states, and declare one legal stroke-radius range read alike by capture, storage and compile.
extra_context: Wave 1, fix. Two contract mismatches in the path primitives are cheap, verified defects, independent of the occupancy work above.

The generic parameter check (`modules/descriptor.rs`'s `ParameterKind::Points` case, against the `points` parameter `mask/commands.rs` declares with `points_max = POINTS_PER_STROKE`) refuses a posted path longer than 1,024 positions before `Stroke::capture` ever decimates it. docs/design/masking.md says the limit is "1024 after decimation" and that an agent may post a raw, undecimated path, so a raw 2,000-position path that would decimate under the limit is refused today for a reason the design does not intend.

The stroke radius has three different legal ranges depending which code reads it: `path.rs`'s `SIZE_MIN..SIZE_MAX` (about 6e-5 to 2), `mask/commands.rs`'s declared parameter range `DISTANCE_MIN..SIZE_MAX`, and `mask/brush.rs`'s own check at `DISTANCE_MIN..DISTANCE_MAX` (64) — three different maximums for what should be one number.
Current shapes only: there is no stored data to migrate, only which check runs where and which range it reads.

Keep the two checks conceptually distinct — a posted path is checked generously before decimation, and the decimated stroke is checked at 1,024 positions after — rather than collapsing them into one number that would reintroduce one or the other defect.

tasks.description: Bind each generated mask control to its parameter's declared kind instead of assuming Number, validate the host mask descriptor like any module's, and correct the docs' "one module and one row" claim.
extra_context: Wave 2, finish the consolidation. This gets the kind table into the shape the next mask kinds need, without building any of those kinds yet.

`CONTROLS` in `mask/commands.rs` builds a `Control::number(...)` for every parameter every geometry kind declares (`declared_geometry_kinds`, `component_parameters`), with no check of the parameter's own declared kind. Every kind today is all-numeric, so this is latent, but a kind whose geometry includes a `points` parameter — the polygon proposed next — would silently get a broken number control for its vertex list.

The host's mask descriptor (`mask::commands::descriptor()`) is deliberately never passed to `ModuleRegistry::register`, so it never reaches `ModuleDescriptor::validate` the way every `ToolModule`'s descriptor does: it is the one descriptor in the system exempt from the rules it asks modules to meet.

docs/design/masking.md says twice that a new kind is "one module and one row" (component kinds, and the desktop's drawn-kind table). docs/design/masking-workspace.md's own polygon proposal shows that is not true for a kind whose geometry is not a flat list of numbers, or that needs an artifact binding: a polygon alone touches about 24 places across roughly 20 files, because `ShapeEditor` and `MaskHandle` are numbers-only and closed, the canvas knows only two gesture families, and the kind table's `Binding` carries no artifacts for a model-based kind to bind at compile time.

Do only the three cheap, safe parts now — filtering `CONTROLS` by parameter kind, validating the host descriptor, and correcting the docs — and record the rest (a JSON-geometry `ShapeEditor`, pointer semantics owned by each editor, a wider `Binding`, artifact discovery from mask components) in masking-workspace.md as what a new kind still needs; none of it is built until a kind is authorized.

tasks.description: Cut paint latency at its measured cause: offer at most one new paint position per presented drafted frame, hand the proxy frame over before the overlay grid is filled, and measure with a feathered brush.
extra_context: Wave 3, speed. A byte-identical speedup that needs a before-and-after figure recorded with scope in docs/specs/performance.md.

The recorded attribution already shows the mask mathematics is not the cause: the worker render is 4.6/5.4 ms p50/p95 and `draft.set` is 0.04 ms, while request-to-worker-start is 6.6/18.2 ms and the pre-result residual is 7.3/20.3 ms. This task should record the per-point mask work (index build, hashing, recompiles) as a non-cause so nobody re-optimizes it later.

Two real causes are in the code path: every `CursorMoved` re-decimates and re-serializes the whole captured path on the desktop (`mask_canvas.rs`, `mask_draft/brush.rs`), and `draft.set` (`api/methods.rs`) validates the whole path and echoes it back, after which planning re-captures and re-hashes it again (`editor/plan.rs`, `mask/commands.rs`) — work proportional to the whole path, roughly eight times per pointer event, so a stroke's per-event cost grows with its length even though the workload's collinear path decimates to 2 points and never shows it.

Separately, in `preview/worker.rs`'s job runner, the mask overlay's coverage grid is computed and attached to the proxy `PreviewResult` before that result reaches `running.send`, so the overlay sits ahead of the frame reaching the screen instead of following it in a second message.

The workload itself hides the second cause: `xtask/src/editor_latency.rs`'s `PAINT_FEATHER` is 0.0, which makes the brush hard-edged and forces the 2×2 proxy supersample (`mask/brush.rs`, `mask_field.rs`) — the opposite of its own comment, which says a hard edge keeps the profile cheap.

Coordinate with whoever measures the drafted job's own full-resolution exact phase, a competing candidate cause, so each figure is attributed to the right change; coverage mathematics are untouched here and renders stay byte-identical.

tasks.description: Write only the strokes captured since the entry's recipe was last read on each commit, and hash a hydrated stroke once instead of twice.
extra_context: Wave 3, speed. A byte-identical speedup with its own before-and-after figure.

`store_strokes` (`editor/catalog.rs`) re-serializes and `INSERT OR IGNORE`s every stroke the recipe's whole mask table references (`Recipe::stroke_references`, which walks every mask and every component, not only the ones this commit touched) on every entry write — O(references) per commit and O(n²) CPU over a session, even though the SQL is a no-op for a stroke already stored. At the measured 1,809-stroke ceiling (docs/design/masking.md "Stroke storage", docs/specs/performance.md) that is an estimated 9–18 ms of owner-thread time per commit, and 1–3 ms at a few hundred strokes: the growth the content-addressed store removed from stored bytes reappears as CPU time.

Separately, `hydrate_strokes` hashes each resolved stroke twice: once in `Stroke::from_stored`'s content-address check and again in `StrokeTable::insert`, which recomputes the stroke's id from the same bytes.
Catalog bytes must stay identical: `INSERT OR IGNORE` semantics are kept, so writing only the strokes captured since the recipe was read changes what work happens, not what ends up stored.

The existing painting-session measurement (`measure_mask_growth_across_a_painting_session` in `editor/catalog.rs`) times reopen and reports catalog size but not per-commit write time; extend it, or add beside it, to record commit time across a long session before and after this change.

tasks.description: Dispatch every mask command through an exhaustive MaskOp enum instead of a method-string match, replace the five-value Planned tuple with a named struct, and split mask/commands.rs by concern.
extra_context: Wave 4, structure. This follows once the kind table is ready for new kinds, so the split lands on a settled shape.

`plan` in `mask/commands.rs` dispatches the generated geometry and sample methods cleanly through `command.geometry`/`command.samples`, but falls through to `match command.method { "mask.delete" => .., "mask.rename" => .., "mask.duplicate" => .., .. other => .. }` for every kind-independent command, with a string fallback arm. `Planned`, what one command touched, is an unnamed five-value tuple built at over a dozen call sites, which invites a positional mistake the compiler cannot catch.

`mask/commands.rs` is about 3,400 lines: roughly 800 of declaration (the COMMANDS table, CONTROLS, the descriptor), 800 of planning, 130 of listing and result types, 200 of helpers and 1,400 of tests. The old JSON-versus-in-process command path is already gone, so what remains here is what stays, just not yet organized by concern.
Two small cleanups in the same file: `unknown_kind` only forwards to `rules::unknown_kind`, and the desktop's `app/masks.rs` hand-copies `MaskTarget::insert_into` instead of calling it.
No behavior change: this is a dispatch and file-shape change over the same commands, the same COMMANDS table and the same `schema.list` output.

tasks.description: Let each mask kind validate its parameters against its own declared ranges instead of hand-checking them again, and share one bounds-to-region helper between brush and radial.
extra_context: Wave 4, structure. Cleanup inside the kind modules, sequenced after the occupancy fix since both touch the brush's compile path.
`linear.rs`, `radial.rs` and `range.rs` hand-write range checks that restate ranges their own declared parameters already state, instead of validating a payload against `parameters(true)`.

The roughly 25-line block that turns a feathered floating bounding box into an integer Region — the grow_low/grow_high closures, the is_finite guard, the whole_stage/empty_region fallbacks — is byte-identical between `mask/brush.rs`'s box-bounds function and `mask/radial.rs`'s ellipse-bounds function, differing only in the earlier lines that compute the box from different inputs (corner points versus centre and extent).
Several kinds also implement `ComponentField` only as inherent methods plus a trait impl that forwards to them, one extra layer with nothing behind it.

No product change: bounds stay conservative (the existing bounds-never-excludes-a-non-zero-pixel tests guard this), and refusal wording may change to the generic check's wording, which current shapes only allows.

tasks.description: Move the mask, brush and range studies into the reference crate's own studies binary, and delete the production tests that re-prove properties bit-identity already covers.
extra_context: Wave 5, tests. A move plus a deletion, independent of the other masking work.

`crates/luxforge-core/tests/mask/study.rs` (1,081 lines), `brush_study.rs` (986) and `range_study.rs` (1,381) — 3,448 lines and 66 tests in all — import only `luxforge_reference` and its reference-typed helpers; no `luxforge_core` item appears in any of them, and `range_study.rs`'s own header already says the binary "shares no code with luxforge-core's production sources." Every other independent study (mixer, presence, tone, vignette, colour, white balance, exposure) already lives in `crates/luxforge-reference/tests/studies/`; these three are the exceptions, so they rebuild and relink as part of the core's `mask` test binary — about 31% of its 11,300 lines — on every core edit that touches nothing they use.

Separately, roughly 330 lines of production tests in `tests/mask/radial.rs` and `tests/mask/brush.rs` re-prove algebraic properties — a feather of zero is a hard edge, invert is the exact complement, a circle is a circle at every aspect ratio, strokes commute — that the studies already prove on the reference, and that bit-identity to the reference (already tested over randomized payloads and whole small stages) already carries over to production.

No product change and no coverage loss: keep every kind's bit-identity tests, move the studies as they are including their ignored figure tests, and update docs/engineering/development.md's description of the mask test binary to match.

tasks.description: Write one kind-conformance test suite driven by a per-kind adapter, delete the mask command-contract tests that now duplicate the field-patch conformance suite, and remove masked-edit tests it already proves.
extra_context: Wave 5, tests. Sequenced after the typed command dispatch so the suite this task writes is tested against a settled shape.

The same per-kind checklist — bit-identical to the reference on random and small-stage payloads, bounds never exclude a non-zero pixel, an off-frame shape bounds to nothing and an inverted one to the whole stage, validation names the field, min_feature_px is the measured ramp, the kind table claims the kind, a sample equals the rendered byte — is written out by hand in `tests/mask/unit.rs`, `radial.rs`, `brush.rs`, `range.rs` and again inside `mask/mod.rs`'s own tests: about 1,500 lines across five places for four kinds.

`mask/command_contracts.rs` (1,806 lines) was written when the JSON path and the in-process path were two separate implementations; since a prior change made `Direct::run` call the same `EditorService::run_action` the JSON path already reaches, its parity test and driver compare that one function with itself, and its retry test re-proves generic deduplication already tested elsewhere. It is a `#[cfg(test)]` module inside `src/`, so it cannot use the shared JSON test client and carries its own.

Masked-edit tests overlap the field-patch conformance suite, which already drafts, commits and updates a masked layer for every maskable module through JSON: parts of `tests/mask/masked_edit_end_to_end.rs`, `masked_colour.rs`'s schema check, and part of `editor/masks.rs`'s own mask-target test duplicate what that suite proves once for every module.

No product change: keep each kind's genuinely distinct tests (the radial's rotated box, the brush index and occupancy, range's value-basedness), the draft-lifecycle tests, and the mask-order and non-maskable-action refusal tests that nothing else covers. Run the old and new suites side by side with the same seeds before deleting anything.

tasks.description: Generalize the path primitives so a second stroke-carrying consumer can share them: a content-addressed store keyed by consumer-declared stroke types, and draft targets from declared identity parameters.
extra_context: Wave 6, roadmap groundwork.
Blocked: starts with the Corrections brush-based repair work; do not begin until that work starts.

Today `path.rs` — meant to be a host primitive with no mention of masks — imports `mask::{REFINE_MAX, REFINE_MIN}` and defines `ColourLimit` as "the pixel the operation the mask modulates receives." The desktop's brush gesture (`mask_draft/brush.rs`) hard-codes the `mask.add-stroke` method by name, and the core `Draft.target` field is typed as an optional `MaskTarget`, so no other module's identity can be a draft target. docs/design/masking.md and docs/design/corrections.md both describe these primitives as already shared, which the code does not yet support.
Masks must keep working unchanged once the primitives generalize: the same content-addressed store, the same stroke addresses, and bit-identical coverage.
Update docs/design/masking.md and docs/design/corrections.md to describe the shared primitive as the code now actually supports it.
